eventMetadata.context_description: Official observations from the Hong Kong Observatory confirm a daily maximum of 27°C on May 15, locking in the market’s 100% consensus on that outcome. Persistent cloud cover, relative humidity of 83–89%, and widespread thundery showers linked to a low-pressure trough limited surface heating and kept temperatures from climbing toward the seasonal mid-May average of 28–31°C. This subtropical pattern, typical when the southwest monsoon begins to influence the region, produced stable conditions that suppressed the usual diurnal rise. Only an unexpected rapid clearing of skies combined with calm winds and reduced moisture could have pushed readings higher, but no such shift materialized in the official data.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent northerly airflow across the UK has anchored London's maximum temperature near 15 °C on May 16, with the latest Met Office and European ensemble guidance converging on this value after holding daytime readings 2–3 °C below the mid-May climatological average of 17–18 °C. Light winds and extensive high cloud have suppressed solar heating and blocked any transient warm advection that might occur under a southerly regime. This setup has produced the overwhelming market-implied probability for exactly 15 °C. A modest shift toward clearer skies or a brief southerly component late in the day remains the primary scenario that could lift readings to 16 °C, though current model consensus assigns low likelihood to such evolution before the daily peak is recorded.

Trader consensus has converged on 33 °C and 34 °C as the most probable outcomes because historical May records and ensemble guidance indicate only modest day-to-day variability of 1–2 °C, driven primarily by local convection timing and wind patterns rather than large-scale shifts. Resolution depends on the official Malaysian Meteorological Department observation at the central station, which will capture the precise peak under standard screening protocols.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Manila’s peak temperature on May 18 is expected to hover near the seasonal May average of 33–34 °C, with the 34 °C outcome commanding the highest market-implied probability. Mid-May typically features peak solar insolation before the southwest monsoon fully establishes, and current PAGASA guidance plus ensemble model runs show light winds and partly cloudy conditions that limit afternoon mixing while allowing surface heating to reach 34–35 °C. Recent observations of 36 °C on May 15 reflect a short-term heat surge tied to suppressed convection, but longer-range guidance indicates gradual moisture return that should cap further intensification. Resolution hinges on the official automated reading at the Science Garden station in Quezon City, where even small shifts in cloud cover or wind direction could swing the daily maximum by one degree.
